subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Reading in detail: comprehension and reasons for over-shopping / Guessing vocabulary from context and make/do collocations
outcomes: Read an article in detail and explain why people over-shop
Guess the meaning of new words from context
Use collocations with make and do correctly

tf.s: The women in the article can spend a lot because they have very good jobs.
tf.why: Yes, one is a corporate lawyer and one is an accountant.

tf.s: Katy feels bad about spending because she thinks it is wrong.
tf.why: Katy feels she deserves a treat for working hard.

tf.s: Clever marketing by companies is one reason people buy things they don't need.
tf.why: Correct, marketing persuades people to buy.

tf.s: The writer says shopping is a long-term solution to feeling bad.
tf.why: It is only a short-term fix that can create debt.

tf.s: A lack of financial self-restraint can lead to bankruptcy.
tf.why: Yes, spending too much can ruin people financially.

tf.s: We say 'make a mistake', not 'do a mistake'.
There is a simple rule that tells you when to use make or do.
tf.why: There is no rule, so we learn these collocations by heart.

tf.s: The words before and after an unknown word can help you guess its meaning.
tf.why: Yes, these context clues give hints.

tf.s: A 'collocation' is two or more words that often go together.

boxes.why: People shop for consolation when they feel lonely.

boxes.q: Why doesn't Katy feel bad about spending?
o: she thinks she deserves a treat
boxes.why: She feels she earned a treat by working hard.
Affluent people have plenty of money.
Spending too much leads to debt.

boxes.q: What helps you guess an unknown word?
boxes.why: Context clues come before and after the word.

boxes.q: Why must you learn make/do collocations by heart?
boxes.why: Without rules, memory is the key.

mcq.q: What jobs do the two women in the article have?
o: a corporate lawyer and an accountant
mcq.why: Their good jobs let them spend a lot.

mcq.q: Which two reasons does the writer give for buying things people don't need?
o: clever marketing and a need for consolation
mcq.why: Marketing and feeling lonely or depressed push people to buy.

o: the washing-up, a favour, some exercise
a mistake, a promise, a joke
the shopping, your duty, a crossword
a favour, the washing-up, a joke

mcq.q: Complete: She ___ a promise to her mother.
mcq.why: Promise goes with make: made a promise.
We say do someone a favour.

mcq.q: 'After losing his job, he went shopping for consolation.' What does 'consolation' mean here?
mcq.why: The context (losing his job) shows he needed comfort.

mcq.q: Why is shopping called a 'short-term fix'?
o: it improves mood briefly but can cause long-term problems like debt
it takes a short time to walk to the shops
it only happens in the morning
mcq.why: The good feeling ends but the debt stays.

mcq.q: What can a lack of financial self-restraint result in?
mcq.why: The article warns about these serious results.

mcq.q: Katy says 'I deserve a treat.' What does this show about her reason for shopping?
o: she uses shopping as a reward for hard work
she shops because things are cheap
mcq.why: She sees shopping as a reward.
